newsitem.title: JAPAN: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN LEADS SHIGA KOGEN GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN LEADS SHIGA KOGEN GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: Swiss Michael von Gruenigen was leading after the first leg of a World Cup men's giant slalom on Saturday, while Alberto Tomba failed to qualify for the afternoon's second run.
Von Gruenigen, first out of the gate, set a blistering pace down the Mount Higashidate course, finishing in one minute 21.88 seconds.
Austria's Andreas Schifferer was second in 1:22.37, while Swiss Paul Accola placed third in 1:22.45.
Swiss skiers took four of the top seven places.
Italian crowd-pleaser Tomba finished 35th. Only the top 30 skiers qualify for the second run.
Norwegian Kjetil Andre Aamodt, who is chasing speed specialist Luc Alphand of France for the overall crown, was sixth.
Aamodt's teammate Lasse Kjus, defending World Cup overall champion, failed to finish after catching an edge at the bottom of the course.
